investigations.title: Dark Money & Digital Influence
investigations.summary: Paid To Persuade? The Dark Money Behind Political Influencers
investigations.story:
In November 2025, Chairman James Comer announced a formal investigation after reports alleged that the Chorus program paid influencers to amplify Democratic political messaging while restricting disclosure of those financial relationships.
The Oversight Committee specifically claimed the program may have:

Circumvented Federal Election Commission disclosure requirements
Blurred lines between journalism and paid political advocacy
Used confidentiality clauses to conceal financial arrangements
Coordinated messaging while avoiding traditional campaign-ad labeling requirements

According to the Committee letters, contracts reportedly:

Restricted creators from disclosing partnerships without approval
Required oversight of political bookings/interviews
Controlled how certain political content could be produced or distributed.
findings: Finding #1. WIRED reported that the Chorus Creator Incubator Program, backed through the Sixteen Thirty Fund, offered Democratic-leaning influencers up to $8,000/month under contracts with secrecy/disclosure restrictions.
Finding #2. The House Oversight Committee opened an investigation in November 2025, saying the program reportedly paid participants to promote Democratic messaging under secrecy contracts.
Finding #3. On May 14, 2026, the Committee said it subpoenaed Sixteen Thirty Fund documents after limited compliance.
